title: observability: propagate request_id + W3C traceparent through streaming API, add per-endpoint metrics tags, OpenAI-compat mapping
author: Arielle Kim
description:
Summary: Add consistent request ID propagation and W3C traceparent handling across the API surface (sync + streaming), include request_id and trace fields on structured logs, and enrich per-endpoint metric labels. Also map OpenAI compatibility headers to Redwood tracing fields so users of the OpenAI-compat layer get the same observability.

Motivation: Customers debugging production streaming sessions often lack a single identifier to correlate logs, metrics, and traces for streaming responses (SSE / websocket / chunked HTTP). This makes incidents and user support slow. Additionally, the OpenAI-compatibility layer introduced a separate header surface (Openai-Request-Id) which wasn't consistently bridged into our tracing/logging stack.

What this PR changes (high-level):
- Propagate request identifiers (accept X-Request-ID, Redwood-Request-Id, OpenAI-Request-Id) and normalize into an internal request_id that is attached to: initial HTTP response headers, all streaming chunk events (SSE + websocket frames), server-side structured logs, and emitted metrics as a tag.
- Accept and forward W3C traceparent/tracestate headers; ensure trace context is injected into downstream RPCs and also included on streaming events so external tracing systems can stitch spans.
- Add per-endpoint metric tags: route (api/chat, api/completions, api/embeddings), compatibility_mode (openai|redwood), model, and streaming=true/false. These are low-cardinality tags intended for aggregation.
- OpenAI-compat: map Openai-Request-Id -> reda_request_id and map OpenAI style telemetry to our trace headers so users of the compatibility layer get consistent IDs.
- Structured logs: ensure the JSON logger includes request_id, trace_id, span_id, route, model, and function_call context (if present). Logs emitted during stream lifecycle (start, chunk, error, end) now include these fields.
- Tests: add unit + integration tests for SSE and websocket transports to assert request_id and traceparent appear on every chunk/event and are present in logs.
- Docs: update observability and openai-compat docs with header mapping and example troubleshooting steps.

Backward compatibility: All header acceptance is additive. If no request ID/traceparent is provided, the server will generate a stable request_id per inbound request. OpenAI-compat header mappings are opt-in via the compatibility_mode flag at the route level.

Migration notes: No migration required. Operators who rely on metric dimensions should update dashboards to account for the new tags (route/model/compatibility_mode/streaming).

redwood/openai_compat/adapter.py - map Openai-Request-Id -> Redwood-Request-Id and inject traceparent into compat responses
redwood/observability/trace.py - parse and normalize W3C traceparent/tracestate, inject to downstream RPCs
redwood/observability/logging.py - structured logger schema update (request_id, trace_id, span_id, route, model, function_call)
redwood/metrics/tags.py - add endpoint-level metric labels and helpers to apply tags atomically
redwood/tests/test_streaming_trace.py - integration tests for SSE + websocket asserting ids in chunks and logs
docs/observability/openai-compat.md - document header mappings and examples
review_comments: Sam Turner (2025-11-14): Nice consolidated approach. A couple of questions: 1) For SSE/ws chunks we need to keep payload overhead minimal — can we avoid repeating full traceparent on every chunk and instead include only request_id with a single traceparent on the first event? I worry about perf on high-throughput streams.

Nadia Patel (2025-11-15): Please add integration tests for websocket transport (we had a bug earlier where middleware was only wired for SSE). Also add a unit test for the OpenAI header mapping behavior.

Ethan Li (2025-11-16): Linter catches and minor naming concerns in streaming_context. Also suggest clarifying the metric cardinality guarantees in docs (explicitly note that model label is optional for aggregation).
CI Bot (2025-11-18): unit tests failed (test_streaming_trace::test_sse_ids) - expected traceparent on chunk but implementation only set it on initial response.
author_responses: Arielle Kim (2025-11-18): Thanks Sam/Nadia/Ethan — addressed: 1) Changed approach to include request_id on every chunk and traceparent only on the first chunk for SSE/ws to reduce event size. Trace context is still available for trace systems via the initial chunk. We also inject traceparent into internal RPC headers for server-side tracing. 2) Added websocket integration tests and updated test expectations. 3) Fixed linter issues and clarified docs regarding metric cardinality.
Arielle Kim (2025-11-20): CI flake: added retry for a timing-sensitive test and removed a brittle sleep in streaming_handler that caused intermittent ordering issues.
ci_checks: unit-tests: pass (initial run failed, rerun after tests/value-fix passed)

release_notes: Added request_id + trace propagation for streaming endpoints; structured logs now contain request_id and trace fields; per-endpoint metric tags (route/model/compatibility_mode/streaming) available for low-cardinality aggregation. OpenAI-compat header mapping ensures Openai-Request-Id is bridged to Redwood request ids.
